_comment_plant: Which implementation of IFSDSPlant stands behind the car. 'chaos' = Chaos observes the car it is already integrating (the only validated reference). 'shadow' = Chaos still DRIVES and the FMU is stepped alongside it with identical inputs, with divergence logged once a second; behaviour is unchanged by construction because nothing downstream reads the shadow. 'fmu' = the FMU is the plant, but the pawn is still Chaos-integrated, so the sensors describe a different car from the one on screen — bring-up only until the Phase 6 kinematic swap. See docs/fmu_plant_migration.md.

Plant._comment_shadowsync: Force the shadow's PLANAR state (x, y, yaw and the planar velocities) equal to the reference's every step, so the comparison asks 'same state, same inputs, same response?' instead of 'how far apart do they drift?'. The drift question cannot be answered by an open-loop shadow at all — the controller is steering the reference, so the shadow diverges without bound however good it is. Vertical state is deliberately NOT synced: the two plants do not share a ride-height convention and the suspension is 56,900 N/m per corner, so injecting the reference's z inflates Fz, inflates mu*Fz with it, and produced 12-14 g of phantom lateral force. Set false only to watch a shadow run free, which is a demo rather than a measurement.

_comment_environment: Trackside environment (docs/ENVIRONMENT_ROADMAP.md). When Enabled, loading a track also loads the <track>.env.json sidecar next to its CSV: ground extent and props, generated in Python from a seed and a profile (docs/environment_sidecar.md). Off by default so the flat world stays the regression baseline; while off, a sidecar is ignored, except a venue track's (profile venue_<venue>, docs/venues.md), which always loads.

VehiclePhysics._comment_motor: MotorMaxTorque, MotorMaxPower, MotorRPM[], MotorTorque[] are vestigial. Drive torque comes from the dedicated UEmraxMotor class (EMRAX 228 MV at 400 V bus, see Plugins/FSDSPlugin/Source/FSDSPlugin/Public/EmraxMotor.h). The pawn silences Chaos's ICE-style engine each tick (SetThrottleInput(0)) and injects per-wheel torque via SetDriveTorque, so these fields feed only the silenced Chaos engine and have no effect on actual driving. Of the motor-side settings, MaxRegenTorque/MaxRegenPower and MotorMaxPower (the drive power cap, 80 kW per the FS rules) are forwarded to the EMRAX class; MotorMaxTorque and the curve arrays are not, peak torque comes from the EMRAX envelope. Kept here so existing tooling and external mirrors keep parsing; remove in a future pass.
VehiclePhysics._comment_regen: Regen is the ONLY braking channel on this car — there is no hydraulic service brake, and EBS is a separate pneumatic system on the handbrake channel. These two therefore define the entire service-deceleration authority of the vehicle. They were previously C++ defaults in FSDSSettings.h with no entry here, which meant the braking model was inheriting numbers nobody had chosen. MaxRegenTorque is the motor-side negative-torque cap; MaxRegenPower is the battery cell input-current limit and is the binding constraint at most speeds. 11000 W is the IFS-08 pack's charge limit: 95s6p Sony VTC6, 5 A max continuous charge per cell (Sony's own standard charge is 3 A; 5 A is the cell's maximum, the cells were not chosen for regen) = 30 A at ~370 V. It was 6000 W, about the 3 A standard charge, which held braking to ~2.5 m/s² at 10 m/s. Near full charge the 4.2 V cell limit allows less, so regen at 100% SoC is lower on the real car.
VehiclePhysics._comment_rolling: Rolling resistance coefficient. Absent until now, which the shadow FMU exposed twice over: a parked FMU car crept at ~1.5 mm/s because nothing opposed motion at zero slip, and on the same throttle that holds Chaos at 3.0 m/s the FMU reached 8.1 m/s mean. The FMU applies it as a resistive WHEEL TORQUE, Crr*Fz*Rw, which is the actual mechanism (contact-patch pressure shifting forward). Chaos has no rolling resistance, so the Chaos plant applies the same Crr*(m*g + downforce) as a body force opposing velocity. 0.020 is typical for a racing slick on warm tarmac; it is an ASSUMPTION, not measured on the IFS-08.
VehiclePhysics._comment_ebs: EBS torque per wheel = EbsGripMultiple * TireMu * (Mass*g/4) * WheelRadius, about 286 N.m, the same formula as matlab/plant/ifssim_params.m. Before this it was the Chaos engine default of 3000 N.m, about 15x the grip limit. EbsFillTime is a linear ramp from 0 to full torque, in seconds; 0 is instant, matching the MATLAB plant. Both are ASSUMPTIONS until measured on the car, and the fill time is the one that decides stopping distance.

Sensors._comment_imu: BMI088 as the car's uDV reads it: 400 Hz on a hardware timer, gyro ±2000 °/s (LSB 1.064 mrad/s, 1 kHz ODR, 116 Hz filter), accel ±6 g (LSB 1.796 mm/s²) at a 100 Hz ODR (ACC_CONF 0xA8), so each accel value repeats 4 times on /imu. /imu is not bias-corrected. Per-axis white noise is fitted from raw BMI088 logs (2026-09-29, 6 stationary power-ups, Allan deviation): accel 2.03/2.78/2.75 mm/s²/√Hz -> σ 0.018/0.025/0.025 m/s² per 100 Hz update (40 Hz filter), gyro 0.32/0.39/0.15 mrad/s/√Hz -> σ 0.0049/0.0059/0.0023 rad/s per 400 Hz sample (116 Hz filter); the gyro x/y values match the car's parked /imu (4.8/4.7 mrad/s). Turn-on gyro offsets were +1.8/+1.7/−0.7 mrad/s on the logger and −3.4/−1.1/−2.6 mrad/s in the 2026-09-20 car bag, so a fresh draw of σ 2.5 mrad/s per session; the car's |g| read 0.9 % low, so accel σ 0.05 m/s². AccelNoiseStd/GyroNoiseStd stay the scalars the bridge publishes as covariance, equal to uDV's (8.25e-4, 1.37e-5). In-run bias drift is still Ornstein–Uhlenbeck with τ 100 s: the logs are too short to fit it.

Lidar1._comment_lidar: Hesai ATX_S01 datasheet (Section 1.4): 1-D rotating mirror (hybrid solid-state), 116 ch, 120° H × 18.3° V FoV (-12.4° to +5.9°), 10 Hz, ~1.74 M pts/s @ 0.08° H, 3 cm 1σ range. PointsPerSecond is the datasheet rate; the LiDAR stream is UDP-only since #322 (TCP and UDS senders retired — pre-#321 they existed to bypass macOS Docker Desktop's ~7 MB/s TCP loopback cap). At the full datasheet rate a ROS 2 subscriber receives the nominal 10.0 Hz on the GPU path (measured 2026-10-01); the ~7-8 Hz once attributed to DDS fragment loss matches the CPU path's own scan rate at this density (7.7-8.9 Hz). Sensor packs only emit *hits*, so the wire rate is roughly 65 % of attempted rays (e.g. 1.14 M pts/s of valid range returns at 1.74 M attempted).
Lidar1._comment_maxrange: MaxRange in metres. Real Hesai ATX_S01 spec is 200 m. Set to 30 m for the sim because cones past 30 m don't matter for FS detection (max-corridor-width is well under that), and shrinking the per-ray broadphase distance is the cheapest UE5 CPU optimisation we have — Chaos walks the spatial hash for every actor along the ray's path, so a 7× shorter ray cuts the per-ray work by roughly that factor. Bump back to 200 for benchmarks against real-car captures or non-FS scenarios.
Lidar1._comment_mount: Mount aligned with the IFS-08's actual LiDAR position: X=0 (CoG-aligned, just beneath the main hoop), Y=0 (centered), Z=1.10 m (main hoop crossbar height). Previously X=0.5 m / Z=0.9 m was a hood-mount approximation; correcting it shifts the sensor back ~50 cm and up ~20 cm, which changes both the cone-detection range envelope (cones at the rear become visible) and the time-to-first-detection for cones immediately ahead. Verify cone_detection still classifies cluster heights correctly after re-baselining.
Lidar1._comment_mount_pitch: Measured on the car (manual bag 2026-09-20, ground plane fitted to parked and driving scans): the Hesai sits 1.00-1.05 m above the ground, pitched 8.4-8.8 deg down, roll under 0.5 deg. Pitch is the mount tilt in UE convention (negative = down); the 116 channels keep their -12.4..+5.9 deg spread in the sensor frame, so levelled they cover about -21..-2.7 deg and the ground is hit from ~3 m instead of ~5.3 m. Z=1.0 puts the sensor ~1.03 m above the ground: at Z=1.1 a 2026-11-02 sim capture measured 1.13 m.
Lidar1._comment_noise: Fitted to the car's Hesai (manual bag 2026-09-20, 40 parked scans, cells matched by ring and 0.1 deg azimuth): sigma = (RangeNoiseStd + RangeNoiseRangeCoeff*r^2) * (RangeNoiseRefReflectance/rho)^RangeNoiseReflectanceExp, clamped x0.3..x4. Car: 1.5 cm at 5-10 m, 1.9 cm at 10-15 m, 4.6-6.7 cm beyond 15 m; 4.5 cm on ~5 % reflectivity, 0.7 cm on ~45 %. EdgeOutlierRate: mixed returns at >30 cm depth edges (car: >30 cm jumps on ~2 % of object returns at 5-10 m; 0.1 per edge ray is a first guess to tune). IntensityNoise: relative jitter (car ~14 %). DropoutRate stays 0.01: the car flickers on ~6 % of cells, but on particular surfaces, not at random.
Lidar1._comment_lidarpath: GPU path (#223): depth render of the scan envelope, async GPU→CPU readback, compute-shader decode. Default at the datasheet 1.74 M pts/s on every platform. Measured on Windows (RTX 3080, same track and driver): 10.0 Hz, sim 60 fps, readback 17 ms median / 34 ms p95 over PCIe, 4.3 cm mean cone position error. The CPU path ('cpu': ParallelFor + Chaos LineTraceSingleByChannel) is kept for parity checks only: at 1.74 M it reaches 7.7–8.9 Hz and smears each scan along the direction of travel (14 cm forward bias), and at 300 k pts/s (the v1.0.0 default) the detector misreads up to 11 % of small cones at 15–20 m as big orange, which trips the stop latch. Do not judge perception below the datasheet density.
Lidar1._comment_perchannelmaxrange: Per-channel max-range overrides in METRES, indexed by V channel (0 = lowest V angle = -12.4°, 115 = highest = +5.9°). Real Hesai ATX_S01 has per-beam laser-power variance (datasheet App. A.1.1) — outer channels reach less far than central beams: 60 m bottom rings, 198 m centre, 90 m top. The array below is derived from the datasheet (App. A.1.2 Sorted by Ring IDs) and linearly remapped [60-198 m] → [25-30 m] so it fits under the sim's MaxRange=30 m perf budget while preserving the relative shape. Regenerate with `python3 tools/gen_per_channel_range.py --pretty`. Length must equal NumberOfChannels (116); mismatch logs a warning and falls back to MaxRange. Both CPU and GPU LiDAR paths read from this.
